AMT.thesis_one_line: The world's largest cell-tower landlord, raising guidance twice this year even as management calls 2026 the growth trough before data-center demand reaccelerates it.
kill_criteria: 2027 AFFO/share growth guidance issued below +5% at the Q4 2026 call
net debt/EBITDA rises above 5.0x for two consecutive quarters
CoreSite revenue growth falls below 8% y/y for two consecutive quarters
organic tenant billings growth (ex-DISH) falls below 5% for two consecutive quarters
a further guidance cut (not raise) at any 2026 quarterly release
key_adverse_facts: Management itself frames 2026 as the AFFO/share growth trough (~3% guided growth) - the Q14 triage's 'comp noise, not a demand problem' framing understates a real, disclosed deceleration
Net leverage 4.9x, at the top of AMT's own 3-5x target band
International (ex-US, ex-India) tower economics remain lower-return than the US book
data_conflicts: Q14_triage.json calls the EPS deceleration 'comp noise, not a demand problem'; the Q2 2026 release instead explicitly attributes it to DISH-related churn and elevated refinancing costs, calling 2026 a trough year - a real, management-acknowledged growth slowdown, not noise
AMT.confidence_in_thesis: medium - guidance raise and reverse-DCF support inclusion, but 2027 reacceleration is a forecast, not yet delivered

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for AMT; at ~15.4x 2026E AFFO/share (below AMT's own 18-24x historical band), the price implies roughly flat-to-low-single-digit AFFO growth, at or below my base case of mid-single-digit 2026 growth reaccelerating toward high-single-digit in 2027. [DV03 2026-10-08: restated on FCF after capex and SBC ($3.79bn) and the $7.16 distribution at cost of equity ~8.9%: implied 10-year growth 4.3%-5.3% (FCF) and 6.0%-6.9% (dividends) vs a mid-to-high single-digit base = in line, not below; the original AFFO perpetuity comparison was not like-for-like.]

AMT.scenario_basis: Base: ~$11.00 2026E AFFO/share growing ~7%/yr as DISH churn laps and CoreSite sustains ~15% growth, exit multiple ~17x AFFO (below own 10y median) plus ~3.2% dividend yield; bear assumes multiple compression to 14x on stalled reacceleration; bull assumes multiple re-rates to 20x on delivered reacceleration.

BRK-B.thesis_one_line: Warren Buffett's conglomerate, now run by Greg Abel, who just flipped from 14 straight quarters of net stock-selling to roughly $20 billion of net buying.
kill_criteria: net equity buying reverses to net selling for two consecutive quarters without a stated reason
buybacks drop back below $1B/quarter while cash exceeds $350B
BNSF or Berkshire Hathaway Energy operating earnings decline y/y for two consecutive quarters
an insurance reserve strengthening (adverse development) exceeding $1B in a single quarter
Abel or another key successor departs
key_adverse_facts: Cash pile still $365.5B - even after this quarter's acceleration, capital deployment has only just begun to normalize
Succession/capital-allocation judgment is now concentrated in one CEO with far less track record than Buffett's six decades
Conglomerate discount can persist regardless of underlying earnings quality

[DVH1 2026-10-06] Q2 2026 operating earnings growth of 16% is 68% foreign-exchange swing in the 'Other' line ($1,242M of the $1,823M increase); insurance underwriting -13% and insurance investment income -9%; operating earnings is a non-GAAP measure.
BRK-B.confidence_in_thesis: high - balance sheet quality and this quarter's capital-allocation signal are both primary-sourced and unambiguous

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: [DVH1 2026-10-06] original relied on the buyback signal, not a valuation. Programme tests: P/B 1.45x with cost of equity 8.2% (rf 5.17% + 0.73 x 4.14%) implies sustainable ROE 10.6% vs operating ROE about 6.6% and 2025 net-earnings ROE about 9.3% (price at or above recent returns); operating earnings $48.0bn as cash base implies 4.7%/yr over ten years vs 8-9% base (below). Mixed: in line. INCLUDE -> INCLUDE-SMALL. No V1 row exists.

BRK-B.scenario_basis: Base: operating earnings compounding ~8-9%/yr (float growth, BHE capex build-out, BNSF pricing) with continued buybacks at current pace, no material multiple change on ~1.3-1.4x book; bear assumes capital-allocation paralysis and a market drawdown compressing the multiple; bull assumes sustained aggressive deployment plus multiple re-rating toward 1.5x book. [DVH1 2026-10-06] note: P/B at $505.48 is 1.45x (market cap $1,085.5bn / equity $747.9bn), not 1.3-1.4x.

CB.thesis_one_line: A top-tier global insurer with an 83.8% combined ratio and record investment income, but priced near the top of its own 10-year valuation range just as management flags softening pricing.
kill_criteria: P&C combined ratio deteriorates above 88% for two consecutive quarters
net premiums written growth falls below 1% y/y for two consecutive quarters
a catastrophe-loss quarter exceeding 5 points of combined ratio
adjusted net investment income growth turns negative y/y
P/B multiple re-rates below the 50th percentile of its own 10-year history without a corresponding earnings miss (would flip toward INCLUDE)
key_adverse_facts: Management explicitly flagged 'softening market conditions and pricing pressure in some lines' on the Q2 2026 call - the tailwind behind 18.2% EPS growth is fading
P/B at the 88.7th percentile of CB's own 10-year history, leaving little room for multiple expansion
Q2 2026 revenue of $15.77B missed consensus by ~0.8% despite the EPS beat
CB.confidence_in_thesis: medium - underwriting quality is not in question; the disagreement is entirely about how much of it is already in the price

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: I agree with V1. P/B (1.78x) sits at the 88.7th percentile of CB's own history versus a peer median of 1.79x; V1's bear/base/bull 3yr annualised returns (-6.5%/0.0%/+13.4%) already price continued strong execution. Management's own disclosed pricing softness is the disconfirming signal the near-zero base case is capturing - implied growth is above my base case of mid-single-digit organic growth with a modestly rising combined ratio. [DV07 correction 2026-10-08: implied_vs_base restated from above to in_line; implied ROE 10.9% (P/B 1.71x on BVPS $195.45, Ke 7.6%, g 3%) vs delivered 15.3%.]

CB.scenario_basis: Base: ~$29 2026E core operating EPS growing ~5-6%/yr as pricing softens back toward mid-cycle, combined ratio drifting from 83.8% toward ~87%, exit P/B near current 1.78x plus ~1.2% dividend yield; taken from V1's own bear/base/bull framework (v1_valuation_table.csv, CB row) which I endorse rather than override.
